messages.content: Can you move my next gym session, which is event number 456123, to next Thursday at 4:30 PM? Today is monday 2022-10-20

function.name: reschedule_event
function.description: Reschedule an event to a new date or time, specified in ISO-8601 format. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

event_identifier.description: The unique identifier of the event to be rescheduled.

new_datetime.description: The new date and time for the event in ISO-8601 format, such as '2023-04-15T13:45:00Z'.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to reschedule event number 456123 to next Thursday at 4:30 PM. Today is Monday 2022-10-20. Next Thursday would be 2022-10-27. They want 4:30 PM. We need to provide the datetime in ISO-8601 format. That would be 2022-10-27T16:30:00Z? But we need to consider timezone. The user didn't specify timezone. We can assume UTC? Or local? Usually we might use local time. But we should ask clarifying question about timezone. The user didn't mention timezone. We could ask "Which timezone?" But maybe we can assume local time zone? The user said "next Thursday at 4:30 PM". We can interpret as local time. But we need to convert to ISO-8601 with timezone offset. If we don't know timezone, we can't produce correct offset. So we should ask clarifying question: "What timezone do you want this scheduled in?" Alternatively, we can ask if they want it in UTC. But better to ask clarifying question.

We also need to check if the event exists. The user says event number 456123. We can attempt to call the function to reschedule. But we need to confirm existence. The system may respond with error if not found. But we can try calling the function. But we need to decide whether to call directly or ask clarifying question. The user didn't mention timezone. It's ambiguous. We can ask clarifying question. The user might accept default assumption. But best practice: ask clarifying question. So we will ask: "Which timezone should I schedule it in?"
